class.name: SchemaRecord
class.brief_description: One schema's declaration, the whole of what two peers must agree on.
class.description: Fixed by [method SchemaCore.fix] and never changed again, because a peer that sealed a different order would address a different column by the same index. [br][br]A record is reachable on its own so a declaration with no session to key it still has somewhere to live. [SchemaCore] holds the session-keyed half and [method SchemaCore.record_of] is the door between them. [codeblock] var record := SchemaRecord.new() record.name = &"Mob" SchemaCore.append_column(record, &"pos", SchemaCore.ColumnType.VECTOR3) SchemaCore.append_column(record, &"hp", SchemaCore.ColumnType.U16) SchemaCore.fix(record) # order and shape_hash are fixed here [/codeblock] Re-declaring a sealed record is idempotent rather than an error, because a script reload re-runs every declaration it owns. Open the replay with [method SchemaCore.open_redeclare], walk the same columns through [method SchemaCore.append_column], and close it with [method SchemaCore.fix]. A genuine shape change answers [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED] there instead of silently shifting every index.

method.name: at
method.description: Returns the column at [param column], or [code]null[/code] when the address is invalid.

method.name: column_count
method.description: Returns how many columns this record declares. A record with none is legal and meaningful: as a table it is a tag, and its commits carry membership alone.

members.member: The declared columns in address order, which is also the wire order a [TableCore] frame lays its columns out in. [br][br]Shared rather than copied, so a binding that compiles its own column shapes appends them here and every consumer reads the one declaration. Append through [method SchemaCore.append_column] rather than directly, because that verb is what refuses a duplicate key and what honours [member sealed].

The caller vocabulary for this schema, and the key [method SchemaCore.find] answers. It is folded into [member shape_hash], and for a table it also decides the wire id, since [method TableCore.wire_id] is the name-sorted position among sealed tables.

Whether the declaration is fixed. Sealing is what makes declaration order address order, so a record that could still gain a column has no stable address to hand out and no hash worth comparing. [method TableCore.declare] refuses an unsealed record for exactly that reason.

The shape hash, fixed at [method SchemaCore.fix] and [code]0[/code] before it, because a hash that could move is not a skew check. [br][br]Every table frame carries it, so mid-session script reload skew is caught rather than only join-time skew. [method TableCore.admit_header] is where a frame carrying a different one is refused.
